roleTitle: Digital Product Manager, Developer Tools Platform
jobDescription: The developer tools platform provides the internal build, test and deployment services used by every engineering team. The Digital Product Manager owns the roadmap for the deployment service, prioritises the backlog with platform engineering and the engineering teams that consume it, runs release reviews, and is expected to raise the share of deployments completed without manual intervention, reported against the platform's documented monthly baseline.
requirements: Sets the direction for the deployment service and decides backlog order together with platform engineering and the teams that depend on it.
Chairs the deployment-service release reviews and keeps the decision log.
Raises the share of deployments completed without manual intervention, reported against the documented monthly baseline.
Lines up each release with platform engineering and the consuming teams, keeping a record of who decided dates and rollout order.
Keeps release notes with limitations and on-call hand-over up to date.

evidence.text: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.
Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.

The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.
Lined each release up with the platform engineering manager and the consuming teams; dates and the order in which teams were moved over were the platform engineering manager's decisions.
Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.

Work sample: a year of the monthly deployment report (share of deployments without manual intervention, the baseline and the rollback release marked) together with the decision log for the rollback release; report identifiers are included for tracing.
Reference call with the former platform engineering manager: the intervention numbers are from the monthly deployment report, automated rollback was the candidate's roadmap item, and the dates match.
Recruiter logistics note: two months' notice; open to a product case-study session.

propositions.text: The candidate set the direction for the deployment service and settled the backlog order each sprint with platform engineering and consuming teams.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the roadmap ownership directly.

propositions.text: The candidate ran release reviews for eight deployment-service releases and recorded decisions in the release record.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the release record document the reviews.

propositions.text: Deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, against a documented baseline of 62 percent.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the figures, period, baseline and report; the work sample and reference confirm them.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions for each release are only partly documented in the release notes.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the intervention result as stated for the three months after the rollback release; do not extend it to other services.
followUpTargets: Ask how hand-over conditions were recorded for each release.
